newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa okays new organisation structure.
newsitem.headline: Endesa okays new organisation structure.

text.p: Spanish electricity company Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa) said on Tuesday it had approved a new organisational structure designed to adapt the group to upcoming changes in the sector.

In a statement, the firm said the new structure envisaged an integrated industrial group centred on its six basic lines of business: generation, distribution, marketing to industrial clients, mining, international and diversification.
Endesa would further integrate those lines of business where economies could be gained from their coordination.

The group would be further split into six corporate divisions that would develop global management: Planning and Control, Organisation and Human Resources, Finance, Legal Consultancy, Communication and General Secretary.

"The modifications introduced reflect our willingness to actively anticipate the changes in the competitive environment of the electricity sector established for 1998," the company said in a statement.
Endesa said the organisational changes would ensure the company maintained its leading position in generation and marketing, where competition will be introduced in 1998.
